newsitem.title: USA: NRC to discuss possible fines on ComEd Zion unit.
newsitem.headline: NRC to discuss possible fines on ComEd Zion unit.

text.p: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission plans to meet July 3 with Commonwealth Edison Co to discuss possible fines for "apparent violations" amid a shutdown last February of Unit 1 at its Zion nuclear station, an NRC spokesman said Tuesday.
NRC inspectors found that plant operators and management failed to follow shutdown procedures in moving reactor control rods around during the February 21 shutdown.

"There were no actual safety consequences asosciated with the control rod movements, but the NRC inspection found extensive deficiencies in control room operating practices, poor communications, and inadequate supervision," the NRC said in a notice about the July 3 meeting with ComEd.
"The purpose of the conference is to hear information from ComEd that might affect our enforcement decision," said Jan Strasma, a spokesman for NRC's Region III office.
"Whether or not there will be a fine assessed is what is under consideration by the conference," he said.

The NRC can impose fines of up to $110,000 per violation. The commission has yet to decide whether to treat the problems during the Zion unit 1 shutdown as several violations or a single violation, Strasma said.
A final decision will be made three to five weeks after the conference.
